# lean-pkg blueprint check

run checkdecls on the blueprint's declaration list at HEAD and check claims.yaml against it; exit 0 nothing missing / 1; writes nothing.

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg blueprint check [--decls PATH] [common flags] NAME
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` |   |
| `--decls PATH` | the declaration list, relative to the checkout (default blueprint/lean_decls, written by leanblueprint) |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `blueprint check NAME` | read-only: the blueprint cross-check. It runs [checkdecls](https://github.com/PatrickMassot/checkdecls) (Patrick Massot, Apache-2.0), never a parser of its own: on a clean checkout, `lake build`, then `lake exe checkdecls blueprint/lean_decls` (the list leanblueprint writes from the `\lean{...}` tags); every `NAME is missing.` line is reported. Then claims.yaml at HEAD: a claim whose `decl` the blueprint names must be a declaration checkdecls accepts (else a problem); claims outside the blueprint and blueprint names no claim carries are notes. checkdecls must be a dependency in `lake-manifest.json` at HEAD; without it the command prints the `require` line to add (lean-pkg never edits the lakefile). A package with no `blueprint/` directory and no declaration list is skipped (exit 0). Uncommitted changes to tracked files refuse. Exit 0 nothing missing, 1 a missing name, a claim problem or a refusal; `--json`: `commit`, `skipped`, `reason`, `decls_file`, `declarations`, `missing[]`, `checkdecls {rev, url, pinned}`, `claims {file, present, checked, problems[], outside_blueprint[], blueprint_without_claim[]}`. See [page: blueprint cross-check](../page.md#blueprint-cross-check) | `[--decls PATH]` |

## Examples

Run checkdecls on blueprint/lean_decls at HEAD (after `lake build`) and check that every claim the blueprint names is a declaration checkdecls accepts.

```bash
lean-pkg blueprint check my-proof
```

Sample output:

```text
my-proof: blueprint check at 0123456789ab: FAILED; 2 declaration(s) in blueprint/lean_decls, 1 missing; checkdecls 3d425859e73f
  missing: MyProof.absent_lemma
  claims: 1 claim(s) in claims.yaml name a blueprint declaration
  note: 1 blueprint declaration(s) no claim carries: MyProof.absent_lemma
```

A blueprint kept elsewhere in the repository; the JSON lists missing\[] and the claim cross-check.

```bash
lean-pkg blueprint check my-proof --decls docs/blueprint/lean_decls --json
```
